title: Trove sleep session
description: One line of health/sleep/<source>/YYYY-MM.jsonl: one sleep session (a night, a nap, a rest) as one source observed it. The normalized convergence of every sleep tracker; the source's full-fidelity record stays in its raw file and is joinable by guid. Additive evolution: readers tolerate unknown fields.

day.description: The local date the session belongs to, as the source attributes it: Oura's own `day` (its sleep day turns over at 18:00, so an evening nap lands on the next day); for a source with no such notion, the local date of `end`. Readers group by this, never by the date of `end`. Also the partition key's day.

start.description: RFC3339 local time the session began (got into bed / the tracker started the session)

end.description: RFC3339 local time the session ended

source.description: collector id, identical to the source folder name

guid.description: source-unique id, the dedupe key and the join key into the source's raw file: Oura's sleep record id; for a relay like Apple Health, `<origin-slug>:<start>`

origin.description: the app or device that recorded the session, when the writer is a relay of several (Apple Health's sourceName: "Oura", "Apple Watch", "Pillow"); omitted when the writer is the device itself

kind.description: the source's own classification of the session, where it has one (Oura: long_sleep → sleep, sleep / late_nap → nap, rest → rest); omitted when the source does not classify

asleep_seconds.description: total time asleep, every stage summed; excludes awake time

in_bed_seconds.description: time in bed, `start` to `end`, awake time included

deep_seconds.description: deep (slow-wave) sleep, where the source reports stages

rem_seconds.description: REM sleep, where the source reports stages

light_seconds.description: light sleep, where the source reports stages (Apple's "Core" stage)

awake_seconds.description: time awake inside the session, where the source reports it

extra.description: the source's scalar fields the shape has no column for (Oura efficiency, latency, average_hrv, lowest_heart_rate, average_breath, restless_periods, …). Per-sample arrays (5-minute phases, heart-rate and HRV samples) stay in the raw file, reachable by guid
